The clinical picture of fatigue, severe pruritus, and abnormal liver function tests in a patient with ulcerative colitis and high-risk sexual history is highly concerning for primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) or HIV-associated hepatitis. To differentiate these, I need to assess for signs of cholestasis and autoimmune markers. Do you have any jaundice, dark urine, or clay-colored stools? Additionally, have you noticed any dry eyes or dry mouth recently?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: HIV-associated hepatitis (likely HIV-related cholestatic liver disease).

The negative anti-mitochondrial antibody and elevated alkaline phosphatase make Primary Biliary Cholangitis unlikely. Given your high-risk sexual history and ulcerative colitis, this presentation is most consistent with HIV-associated hepatitis or drug-induced liver injury from medications.
